verses.1: Praise the LORD. Praise the name of the LORD. Praise, you servants of the LORD.
verses.2: Those who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courtyards of the house of our God.
verses.3: Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good. Sing to his name, for it is pleasant.
verses.4: For the LORD chose Jacob for himself, and Israel as his special possession.
verses.5: For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is greater than all the gods.
verses.6: Whatever the LORD desires, he does in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in all the deep.
verses.7: He raises up clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the winds from his storehouses.
verses.8: He struck the firstborn of Egypt, from man to beast.
verses.9: He sent signs and wonders in your midst, Egypt, to Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.10: He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
verses.11: Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
verses.12: And he gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel, his people.
verses.13: The name of the LORD endures forever. The memory of the LORD lasts through all generations.
verses.14: For the LORD judges his people, and for his servants he shows compassion.
verses.15: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
verses.16: They have mouths, but cannot speak. They have eyes, but cannot see.
verses.17: They have ears, but cannot hear, nor is there breath in their mouths.
verses.18: Let them become like those who made them, all who trust in them.
verses.19: House of Israel, bless the LORD. House of Aaron, bless the LORD.
verses.20: House of Levi, bless the LORD. All who fear the LORD, bless the LORD.
verses.21: Blessed be the LORD from Zion, the one who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "Praise the LORD" is a translation of הַלְלוּ יָהּ, commonly rendered "Hallelujah." The form is consistent with the psalm’s liturgical tone.
- v. 15: "Idols" is a contextual interpretation of עֲצַבֵּי הַגּוֹיִם. The term is not explicitly "idols" in Hebrew but is clear in context.
- v. 18: "Let them become like those who made them" reflects the imperative form in the Hebrew, though it may also be read as a declarative statement.

Notes
- v. 1: "Praise the LORD" is a translation of הַלְלוּ יָהּ, commonly rendered "Hallelujah." The form is consistent with the psalm’s liturgical tone.
